A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphRAG-Bench work. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–L are readable and can be matched across versions, including relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation and retrieval evaluations on the Novel and Medical datasets, graph statistics, and token-cost measurements, including additional results in Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains those original evaluations and additionally reports graph construction costs, model-size sensitivity, corpus-size scalability, and statistics for two additional benchmark corpora.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline in Section 3 and Appendix C, question-generation prompts, and evaluated RAG procedures are retained. The added experiments apply existing methods without introducing algorithmic components.

E1.justification: Table 13 extends corpus-structure analysis to MuSiQue and 2WikiMultihopQA. Generation evaluation retains the Novel and Medical domains and the same four task categories; the corpus-size sweep varies data volume within Novel.

E2.justification: Existing generation and retrieval comparator sets remain unchanged. The new indexing-cost comparison in Table 15 includes KGP, KET-RAG, and Lazy-GraphRAG, extending efficiency comparison participation beyond v2's Tables 6–7, although these methods already appeared in other evaluations.

E3.justification: Appendix F changes the stated accuracy weight alpha from 0.5 to 0.75 without explaining whether scores were recomputed. G.3–G.5 substantially extend the evaluation design with indexing measurements on one approximately 56k-token book, a controlled 3B/7B/14B generation-model sweep, and corpus sizes of approximately 56k, 603k, and 1,132k tokens.

E4.justification: G.4–G.5 add sensitivity analyses testing dependence on generation-model capacity and robustness to increasing corpus size. G.3 adds indexing-cost profiling beyond the retained prompt-cost analysis. These address practical deployment and scaling questions not experimentally examined in v2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new experiments continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Retained result values are unchanged, but Tables 15–17 add substantial indexing-cost and scaling results, and Table 13 adds two corpus-statistics rows. For example, KGP records 32.01 seconds and 89,215 indexing tokens; Table 16 reports HippoRAG2 average ACC of 57.08, 61.50, and 63.91 across 3B, 7B, and 14B. These are results under additional settings, not demonstrated performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8) and the definitions of knowledge breadth and reasoning depth are retained, with no added proofs or formal results. The revised default alpha is an evaluation-parameter change; the parameterized accuracy formula remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: a benchmark combining hierarchical reasoning tasks, contrasting corpus structures, and evaluation across the GraphRAG pipeline. The additional evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: G.3–G.5 add substantive deployment and mechanism interpretations: favoring lightweight indexing under resource constraints, proposing a practical 7B minimum model size, and attributing corpus-scale stability to structural filtering by graphs. These extend applicability guidance beyond v2's discussion. Appendix J's text-only limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 discloses graph-count normalization per 10k corpus tokens, reuse of a GPT-4o-mini-built index across model sizes, and tiktoken-based corpus sizing. The reproducibility statement switches to the GitHub repository already cited in v2, while Appendix A.1 removes the explicit leaderboard-site link. Existing baseline configurations remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including FaithfulRAG, adaptive reasoning structures, LAG, reasoning-path distillation, graph-based agent memory, and graph learning/fairness work. These are limited additions to the introduction and Appendix I; the benchmark's novelty argument and positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds the ICLR publication header and three Appendix G subsections, and makes localized edits to the FAQ, reproducibility statement, and citation-bearing passages. The main narrative, terminology, and overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 15–17 and two rows to Table 13. The former implementation Table 15 is retained as Table 18, with appendix floats and page breaks shifting. All ten figures, including the leaderboard and prompt examples, retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The new cost and sensitivity analyses could strengthen practical guidance, and graph-count normalization is clearer. However, v3 changes the accuracy weight while retaining prior scores without explanation. Table 17's Novel/Small RAG row exactly repeats the Medical RAG accuracy values in retained Table 3, and G.4 cites 57.59 where Table 16 reports 57.08. These unresolved reporting inconsistencies weaken confidence in the added evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
